title: Governments pledge to advance territorial rights across 160 million hectares

needs.need: What governments have promised to do, distinguishing newly recognized territorial rights from stronger protection of rights already recognized.
needs.inStory: Its 2030 goal covers 160 million hectares: at least 80 million hectares would receive formal recognition of land rights, while another 80 million hectares with recognized rights would get stronger governance and protection.
needs.accepts: States that the Intergovernmental Land Tenure Commitment targets 160 million hectares by 2030: at least 80 million hectares of formal recognition and a further 80 million hectares of stronger governance and protection for already-recognized rights, naming its source.

example.value: The commitment covers recognition on at least 80 million hectares and stronger governance and protection on another 80 million hectares by 2030.
example.source: IPS Inter Press Service, "Protecting the Climate Means Protecting Territorial Rights" (2026-11-12)

needs.need: How the 80-million-hectare recognition target compares with the amount of Indigenous and community land still lacking legal recognition.
needs.accepts: Gives a named source's estimate of Indigenous and community land held under customary rights without legal recognition, in hectares or as a share of land, with its geographic scope, and relates it to the 80-million-hectare recognition target. A comparison must acknowledge any difference between the estimate's scope and the pledge's countries.

example.value: Indigenous Peoples and local communities hold customary rights to at least half of the world's land but have legally recognized ownership of only about 10%.

needs.need: Whose territorial rights the commitment is meant to advance and which countries have joined it.
needs.accepts: Names the rights-holders (Indigenous Peoples, Afro-descendant and local communities) and at least several of the 17 participating countries or the regions they lie in, with a named source. The locations studied for concession overlaps do not establish where the pledge applies.

needs.need: Whether the announced commitments have translated into funding reaching the communities they are meant to support.
needs.inStory: The land-rights goals and funding are commitments, not evidence that the work has been completed. Reporting after the pledge said funds had been slow to reach affected communities.
needs.accepts: Gives a sourced account of whether pledged funds have reached affected communities, distinguishing a funding announcement from delivery. An attributed report that funds have been slow to reach communities meets the need; repeating the pledged total does not.

example.value: Despite the pledges, funds have been slow to reach affected communities.
example.source: Grist, "Indigenous leaders at COP31 say it's past time to turn promises into action" (2026-11-13)

needs.need: When the territorial-rights targets are due and which years the complementary funding covers.
needs.inStory: committed to advance territorial rights across 160 million hectares by 2030, with separate targets for new recognition and stronger protection where rights already exist. A complementary $1.8 billion pledge for 2026–2030
needs.accepts: States that the territorial-rights targets are due by 2030 and that the $1.8 billion pledge covers 2026–2030, with a named source, as deadlines and funding periods rather than completed work.

example.value: The territorial-rights targets run to 2030, while the complementary $1.8 billion pledge covers 2026–2030.
example.source: IPS Inter Press Service, "Protecting the Climate Means Protecting Territorial Rights" (2026-11-12)

needs.need: The earlier forest-tenure pledge the $1.8 billion follows, and what it delivered.
needs.accepts: Names the $1.7 billion Indigenous Peoples and Local Communities Forest Tenure Pledge made at COP26 in Glasgow for 2021–2025, and relates the new $1.8 billion for 2026–2030 to it; credit for reporting how much of the earlier money reached community organizations directly, with a named source.

example.value: At COP26 in 2021, donors pledged $1.7 billion for 2021–2025 to support Indigenous Peoples' and local communities' forest tenure.
example.source: UK government COP26 announcement; Forest Tenure Funders Group annual reports

needs.need: What summit or announcement brought the commitment forward at this time.
needs.accepts: Identifies the occasion, such as the COP31 climate summit under way in November 2026 where Indigenous leaders pressed for delivery, or the commitment's launch at a named earlier summit, credited to a named source. General pressure on forests or demand for transition minerals does not meet it.

example.value: Indigenous leaders at COP31 urged governments to carry out their land-rights commitments.
example.source: Grist, "Indigenous leaders at COP31 say it's past time to turn promises into action" (2026-11-13)

needs.need: What free, prior and informed consent requires when energy projects affect Indigenous territories.
needs.accepts: Explains that consent must be sought from Indigenous peoples through their own representative institutions, without coercion, before a project is approved, and on the basis of adequate information; distinguishes consent from merely informing or consulting, naming a source.

example.value: States should consult and cooperate in good faith through Indigenous peoples' representative institutions to obtain their free and informed consent before approving projects affecting their lands, territories or resources.
example.source: United Nations Declaration on the Rights of Indigenous Peoples, Article 32

notes: Grist's 400 million acres is about 162 million hectares: the same commitment, not a larger one. The countries and the launch occasion must not be inferred from the concession-overlap research.
